subject: Helix Health private offer: channel passback mechanics and list-price harmonization
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura@helixhealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify AWS private offer economics and partner margin flow

Neha —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement had a few follow-ups before we send the PO to legal: how will the AWS private offer reflect in our invoices, and what does Redwood expect for the channel passback to our systems integrator (PulseBridge)? Specifically:

- Will the invoice originate from Helix (gross-to-net) or will Redwood/Marketplace invoice Helix and route a reseller commission to PulseBridge?
- For list-price harmonization: we operate in multiple US regions and need consistent list prices for our internal chargebacks. Can the private offer keep list prices aligned while applying the agreed discount on the private-offer token level?
- Can you share a draft of the private offer document and a simple example P&L for Year 1 with the reseller margin included?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs this for Wednesday.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Procurement, Helix Health
Procurement: procurement@helixhealth.com

---
Attachment: None (see requested docs)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Laura Kim <laura@helixhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AWS private offer economics and partner margin flow

Laura —

Thanks, and great to connect. Short answers up front, then a small example attached.

- Invoice path: Redwood will invoice Helix directly (Helix is the contracting customer). Reseller commissions to PulseBridge are handled off-invoice via Redwood's partner payout process tied to the private-offer ID; PulseBridge submits evidence and Redwood issues partner payouts per our partner agreement. This keeps your accounting simple (single customer invoice) while preserving a clean channel payout.

- List-price harmonization: yes — we can keep the SKU/list price consistent across US regions and apply the private-offer discount as a marketplace-level override. That means your internal chargebacks see the same list prices; the effective discount is reflected separately.

- Draft and example: attached Helix_PrivateOffer_Draft_v3.pdf and RI_pricing_model_helix.xlsx (Year 1 P&L with a 12% reseller passback line).

Couple of clarifying questions from our side to make the draft precise:
1) Do you want the partner payout to be a % of list price or % of net revenue after Redwood discounts? (We typically recommend % of list to preserve partner economics.)
2) Is PulseBridge the only channel recipient, or should we include a secondary services partner?
3) Are you planning to treat this as committed capacity (node-hour reserve) or purely metered consumption? Committed deals change the waterfall timing for credits.

Putting Karthik and Ben on copy to confirm marketplace routing details and partner payout operational flow.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Strategic Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: Helix_PrivateOffer_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 162KB), RI_pricing_model_helix.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: marketplace routing and payout mechanics for Helix

Team —

Reviewed the draft. Operational points we should confirm with Helix before finalizing the PO/DocuSign:

- Payout base: agree with Neha's recommendation to pay PulseBridge on % of list price. That avoids variability when we apply additional promotional credits. If Helix insists on % of net we need to set clear exclusion rules (e.g., exclude usage credits, onboarding credits).

- Timing: partner payouts run monthly with a 30-day reconciliation lag after invoice payment. If Helix needs faster pass-throughs we can explore a prepaid carveout but that needs procurement sign-off.

- Tax and remittance: reseller passbacks are grossed without tax withholding on our side; PulseBridge will receive an automated payout file that they reconcile against invoices. We should surface this so Helix's accounting can map it to their partner ledger.

- List-price: marketplace supports list-price harmonization across AWS regions when the offer is created as a single private offer. We'll set the "ListPriceID" uniform across the US regions and apply the private discount override. Ops note: that locks the list price until the private-offer expires or is amended — call that out in the offer.

I'll draft one paragraph for the private offer that captures the passback base and timing.

-Karthik
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Laura Kim <laura@helixhealth.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AWS private offer economics and partner margin flow

Laura —

Thanks for the note — wanted to be transparent about a pragmatic channel structure we've used for other health-tech customers:

- Standard reseller passback: 12% of list price paid monthly after invoice settlement.
- Alternative proposal if Helix prefers lower visible margin: 8% reseller passback + a one-time implementation credit (we can fund up to $60k for onboarding services to PulseBridge), treated as a separate credit line (not reducing the partner payout base).
- Committed option: if Helix wants a 12-month committed block (min monthly spend), we can tier the partner passback up to 14% at higher commit thresholds.

Let me know which route you'd like to pursue. I can update the attached pricing model and produce two P&L scenarios.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Partner GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Kim <laura@helixhealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-26T07:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AWS private offer economics and partner margin flow

Ben/Neha —

Thanks — we like the 8% + $60k onboarding credit option because it preserves our ledger (lower visible commission) while ensuring PulseBridge has funding for initial integration. A few requests before we sign:

1) Can Redwood document that the $60k onboarding credit is contractually earmarked to PulseBridge (so we can show services spend in our audit)?
2) Please include the partner's remit details in the partner payout appendix (PulseBridge EIN and invoice routing instructions).
3) We need the private offer to explicitly state that list prices across US regions will remain unchanged for the offer term (12 months) unless amended by mutual written consent.

If you can update the draft and send back a DocuSign link, procurement will route for signature.

Best,
Laura
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Laura Kim <laura@helixhealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AWS private offer economics and partner margin flow

Laura —

Appreciate the clear direction. Attached is Helix_PrivateOffer_Draft_v3.pdf (redline) updated to: 

- Show $60,000 onboarding credit as contractually designated to PulseBridge (Section 4.2).
- Spell out partner payout: 8% of list price, monthly payout after invoice settlement; PulseBridge remit details added to the partner appendix.
- State list-price harmonization across US regions for 12 months and amendment clause by mutual written consent.

Also uploaded a DocuSign packet to the HubSpot deal record and included the external signing link: https://www.docusign.com/rc/1234-example-sign. Procurement should be able to sign and return.

If that looks good I'll queue legal for final sign-off and we can kick off onboarding with PulseBridge once the executed PO is received.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference
